clue.text: A stiff examination

parts.note: a stiff is slang for a corpse, so this is the medical inspection of a dead body, not a hard exam

explanation.definitionFit: An autopsy is the examination of a corpse, which slang calls a stiff.

clue.text: Jabber, with so wooden a face

explanation.definitionFit: A poker jabs at a fire, and a poker face is expressionless and impassive.

clue.text: Browned off, getting buns undercooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared differently, mixed up

explanation.surface: Bread rolls left in too briefly are getting fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browned off' is British slang for fed up, but here it means tanned. 'cooked' rearranges BUNS and UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunburnt skin has been reddened or tanned by too much sun.

clue.text: Dismissal by the left, for example, to begin with

definitions.text: by the left, for example, to begin with

explanation.definitionFit: Being sacked is getting your notice; By the left, quick march is a parade command starting a soldier's advance.

clue.text: Very happy to make circular angle sort of square

parts.note: a radian is the angle in a circle subtended by an arc equal to the radius
a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to draw a curved angle with a drawing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant means glowing with joy.

clue.text: Community providing power to, rout our team

indicators.note: a rout is a heavy defeat that scatters, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A group delivers energy to crush our side.
explanation.definitionFit: Euratom is the European Atomic Energy Community, a body for nuclear energy.

clue.text: One came across the reverse, also

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the reverse tells us the word for came across is read backwards

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them, past tense met

explanation.surface: Someone encountered the other side of something as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the reverse' turns MET into TEM, placed after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin item means likewise, used in lists for an additional entry, so it is a synonym of moreover.

clue.text: One to be swallowed in abstemious country

indicators.note: swallowed in means the pieces go inside the word for abstemious

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking
one is the Roman numeral I
be is the verb to be

explanation.surface: A drink must be gulped down in a dry land.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a Himalayan region, once an independent nation.

clue.text: Unable to smoke? Perfect!

explanation.definitionFit: Without lucifers you cannot light up; matchless also means unrivalled or peerless.

clue.text: Inmate of a not necessarily military hospital

definitions.text: Inmate of a not necessarily military hospital

parts.words: Inmate of a not necessarily military hospital
parts.note: an inmate of a hospital is someone being treated, and a soldier of lowest rank suggests a military one, though here the word means paying, not state-funded

explanation.definitionFit: Someone treated in a paying, non-state hospital is privately cared for, a pun on the army rank.

clue.text: Bolshie, but not likely to upset his family

parts.note: someone kind is unlikely to hurt or upset you
Bolshie, short for Bolshevik, gives red, a communist

explanation.surface: A man is a stroppy leftie, yet would not offend his relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the reverse of the clue's order. 'Bolshie' is British slang for awkward or rebellious, originally Bolshevik.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred are blood relatives, a man's kin or relations.

clue.text: A little money goes on exquisite snack

indicators.note: goes on means the coin word is placed after the other piece

parts.note: rare in the sense of unusually fine or excellent
a bit was an old British coin, as in threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A small sum is spent on a fine treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes on' puts BIT after RARE. A threepenny bit was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, a light savoury dish.

clue.text: Unrefined actors going to the wall in the dream-play

definitions.text: going to the wall in the dream-play

parts.note: rough means crude or unpolished
the actors in a play make up its cast

explanation.surface: Crude players are going under in a production of a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream the rustic who plays Wall wears plaster and roughcast; 'going to the wall' usually means failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughcast is coarse plaster applied to a wall, worn by the character Wall in Shakespeare's Dream.

clue.text: Against a way to use acid in cattle feed

parts.note: V is short for versus, against
to etch is to engrave a surface with acid

explanation.surface: Someone objects to an acid treatment of livestock food.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetch is a leguminous plant grown as fodder for livestock.

clue.text: Many unattributable works accepted

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
anon, short for anonymous, marks writing with no known author

explanation.surface: Lots of anonymous writings have been accepted as genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer's canon is the body of writings accepted as genuinely theirs.

clue.text: Smoke from garlic oil being cooked

indicators.note: being cooked suggests the letters are mixed as in a recipe

explanation.surface: Fumes rise from garlic fried in oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarillo is a thin small cigar.

clue.text: On occasion, Board provides schedule of work

parts.note: an occasion is a time when something happens
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Now and then a management board issues a work schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or works timetable sets out when each task or lesson happens.

clue.text: Here are the papers for summary hearing

parts.note: brief means short, a summary
a case is a legal hearing in court

explanation.surface: Documents are prepared for a short trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is a flat bag carrying documents.

clue.text: Sponsor transfer of home to GDR

indicators.note: transfer suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A backer arranges a move of house to East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transfer of' rearranges HOME, TO and GDR (the old East Germany).
explanation.definitionFit: A godmother sponsors a child at baptism, vowing to oversee its religious upbringing.

clue.text: Regular a little in the shade

indicators.note: in means the little piece sits inside the shade word

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
a bit means a little

explanation.surface: A frequent visitor sits slightly in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitue is a regular visitor to a place, such as a bar.

clue.text: Is the country about to discover .the truth?

indicators.note: about means the country word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom or country

explanation.surface: Is the nation about to learn what really happened?
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is a faithful depiction of how things actually are.

clue.text: One in Shakespeare's Eastcheap tavern with hollow legs?

indicators.note: with here means having the hollow shape held in among the legs

parts.note: pins is slang for legs
a hollow, empty shape is O

explanation.surface: A drinker in an old London tavern is said to have hollow legs, holding any amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' puts O within PINS. Having hollow legs is a joke about a person who can drink endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Poins is Prince Hal's companion in Henry IV, drinking with Falstaff at the Boar's Head inn.

clue.text: Defied being beheaded and went mad

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: to brave something is to defy it

explanation.surface: Someone defied the executioner and lost their wits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being beheaded' removes the B from BRAVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Raved means ranted wildly, as a lunatic does.

clue.text: Hurrah for exam — student's last

parts.note: a viva is an oral university exam

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word student

explanation.surface: Cheers for a test that comes after a student's final one.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivat is a Latin cheer meaning long may he live.

clue.text: Mock Turtle soup is most appealing

definitions.text: Mock Turtle soup is most appealing

parts.words: Mock Turtle soup is most appealing
parts.note: the Mock Turtle in Alice in Wonderland sings a song praising soup, opening with an adjective for lovely

explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's book the Mock Turtle sings that soup is lovely, the word opening each line.

clue.text: This meditative position you say is held by many

indicators.note: is held by means this piece goes inside the many word

parts.note: lots means many

indicators.note: say tells us to use the letter that sounds like the word you

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Many people hold this yoga pose, you say.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a cross-legged sitting posture used in yoga.

clue.text: Young creature is always allowed outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for allowed surrounds the other piece

parts.note: let means permitted
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A young animal is always allowed to roam out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year.

clue.text: It's not right to demand and get one name put forward

indicators.note: put forward means the one and name pieces go in front

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to exact payment is to demand it

explanation.surface: It is wrong to make demands and get a nominee advanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put forward' sets I and N before EXACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise or slightly wrong.

clue.text: No soda, but Scotch finally taken on a.French tennis court

annotationWithheld.why: No soda, but Scotch finally taken on a French tennis court: the definition is the Tennis Court Oath, but no parse found for the wordplay giving OAT before H
annotationWithheld.clue: No soda, but Scotch finally taken on a.French tennis court

clue.text: Pressure on junction of sewer

indicators.note: on means the pressure word is placed after the junction word

parts.note: a seam is a line where two pieces join
stress means pressure or strain

explanation.surface: Strain is put on where the drains meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' looks like a drain but is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress is a woman who stitches clothes for a living.
